patients.summary: Landscaping supervisor and daily smoker with hypertension, hyperlipidemia and nonobstructive coronary disease who joined in 2022. In 2024 a bleeding gastric ulcer needed operative repair and a transfusion caused an acute hemolytic reaction; in 2025 he had two inferior STEMIs, each stented, and he still smokes.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT. 52M, runs a landscaping crew, here to set up primary care; his last office closed its internal medicine side over the summer and he has been coasting on refills.

Known problems per pt: high blood pressure for years, cholesterol, and a heart scan last year that showed some plaque in one artery. Saw cardiology once for that, told to keep the statin and the BP pill, no stents, nothing further. Denies exertional chest discomfort, dyspnea, palpitations, leg swelling. Gets winded hauling mulch bags up a slope at the end of a long day but no different from the rest of the crew.

Meds: lisinopril 20 daily, atorvastatin 40 daily. Takes both, rarely misses.
Allergies: none to medicines.
PSH: none.
FH: dad had a heart attack at 62. Mom has blood pressure. One brother on a cholesterol pill.
SH: smokes a pack a day, started in his early 20s, so roughly 30 pack-years. A drink or two a month at a cookout. No other substances. Outdoors all season, plows in winter.

Exam: well-appearing, weathered. BP above, recheck similar. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear, no wheeze. Abd benign. No peripheral edema, DP pulses 2+.

A/P
1. HTN on lisinopril 20: a bit above goal today. Home cuff readings requested before changing anything.
2. Hyperlipidemia / CAD (nonobstructive on 2021 CT angio per pt): continue atorvastatin 40. Lipids today. Records request to prior office for the CT report.
3. Tobacco: talked through what quitting would mean for the plaque already there. He is not ready, says the job and the smoking go together. Will keep asking.
4. Lung cancer screening: qualifies by age and pack-years. Low-dose CT ordered.
5. Health maintenance: colonoscopy around 2019 at old office, normal per pt. Hep C and HIV once, A1c screen, CMP, CBC today. Flu shot given.

RTC 6 months or sooner with home BP numbers.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Kevin, your bloodwork from last week is back. Kidney function, liver tests, blood count and sugar (A1c) are all fine. The hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative, so those are done for good. LDL cholesterol on the atorvastatin is acceptable for now; we will recheck next year. The radiology department will call you to schedule the lung CT. Thanks.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Prior PCP records, 38 pages, filed under media.

PCP abstract of the relevant items:
- CT coronary angiography, 03/2021: nonobstructive plaque in the right coronary artery, roughly 40% narrowing; no other significant stenosis. Cardiology consult after it recommended continuing statin and BP therapy, risk factor control, no further testing.
- Screening colonoscopy, 2019: no polyps; repeat in 10 years.
- Tdap 2018.
- Med list matches ours (lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40). No drug allergies listed.
- BP log in the old chart mostly 130s-140s systolic.

Problem list updated; no changes to plan.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text: Indication: lung cancer screening, current smoker, 30 pack-years. Technique: low-dose helical CT of the chest without contrast. Findings: no pulmonary nodules. Airways patent. No consolidation or effusion. Heart size normal. No mediastinal or hilar adenopathy. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable. Osseous structures intact.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1, negative. Continue annual screening in 12 months.

documents.title: Result note
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt with lung CT result per PCP: negative, repeat next fall. He asked if that means the smoking is not hurting him. Explained the scan only looks for cancer and not the damage to the heart or lungs. He laughed and said he figured.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Early slot before the season starts. Home BP cuff readings on his phone, mostly 132-140 over low 80s, one or two in the 140s after a night of bad sleep. No headaches, CP or SOB. Taking lisinopril and atorvastatin. Still a pack a day; tried cutting down over the winter, back to baseline by February.

O: Vitals as charted. Alert, comfortable. RRR, lungs clear. No edema.

A/P:
- HTN: home average a little over goal for someone with coronary plaque. Discussed adding a second agent vs. lifestyle; he wants to see whether the busy season (more walking, less sitting) helps first. Recheck at physical.
- CAD/lipids: on atorvastatin 40, LDL last fall acceptable. No change.
- Tobacco: asked again. Not ready. Handed him the state quitline card.
- Shingrix #1 today; #2 in 2 months, nurse visit.

documents.title: Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Shingrix dose 2 of 2, 0.5 mL IM, left deltoid. Came straight from a job site. Reports first dose gave him a sore arm and chills that night, nothing else. Advised similar is possible. Series complete.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam. 53M.

Interval: nothing new. Busy summer, crew of six. No chest pressure with work, no breathlessness beyond his usual, no claudication. Sleeping ok. Home BP still mostly 130s/80s.

Meds: lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily. NKDA.
Habits: 1 ppd, unchanged. Alcohol rare. PHQ-2 0, AUDIT-C 1.

Exam: Vitals reviewed. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no bruits. Cardiac: regular, S1 S2, no murmur. Chest clear bilaterally. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly. Skin: sun damage on forearms and neck, no suspicious lesions. Extremities warm, pulses intact, no swelling. Neuro grossly intact.

Assessment/plan
- HTN: borderline control at home; he again prefers not to add a drug. Revisit in winter.
- CAD and lipids: atorvastatin 40. Fasting panel today.
- Tobacco use disorder: counseled; declines meds and NRT for now.
- Lung screening: due next month, ordered.
- Vaccines: flu, updated COVID, and PCV20 (smoker under 65) today. Shingrix done. Tdap 2018.
- Colon: 2019 colonoscopy, next 2029.

Follow up in about 4 months.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text: Comparison: 10/2022. Technique: low-dose noncontrast helical chest CT. Lungs: no nodules or masses. No consolidation. No pleural effusion. Cardiomediastinal contours within normal limits. No adenopathy. Upper abdomen and bones unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1. Negative screen; next annual low-dose CT in 12 months.

documents.title: CT result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Kevin, this year's screening CT is clear again. Same plan for next October. The best thing you could do for your lungs and heart is still the cigarettes, whenever you are ready I'm here.
